problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate the distribution of a specialized commodity from a network of regional storage depots to a series of major urban distribution centers, with the objective of minimizing overall freight expenses.

The inventory available at each regional depot (set R) is precisely quantified:
* Depot R1 holds 156 units.
* Depot R2 holds 65 units.
* Depot R3 holds 102 units.
* Depot R4 holds 157 units.
* Depot R5 holds 149 units.

The requisite volume to be delivered to each urban center (set C) is firmly established:
* Center C1 requires 103 units.
* Center C2 requires 123 units.
* Center C3 requires 150 units.
* Center C4 requires 134 units.
* Center C5 requires 66 units.

The per-unit freight charge for routing from each depot to every center is detailed in the following matrix:
| Origin / Destination | C1 | C2 | C3 | C4 | C5 |
|--|-|-|-|-|
| R1 | 1 | 12 | 10 | 13 | 14 |
| R2 | 18 | 18 | 20 | 8 | 16 |
| R3 | 8 | 9 | 14 | 16 | 1 |
| R4 | 13 | 11 | 13 | 6 | 15 |
| R5 | 5 | 20 | 18 | 1 | 13 |

Determine the optimal allocation of shipments to achieve minimal total expenditure.
